prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: In this downward-angled egocentric view, the depth map clearly stratifies the foreground workspace within arm's reach (~0.3–0.6 m) from the dark background floor and wooden chair (~1.2–1.8 m) ahead and to the right. The brightest (nearest) regions are the camera wearer's left hand holding cotton on the left (~0.3–0.4 m) and right forearm entering from the lower right (~0.35–0.5 m), positioned just above a mid-grey circular steel basin (~0.5–0.6 m) resting on the wearer's lap, while a small basket sits lower down to the left (~0.7 m). To the upper left, a second person's partially visible torso/legs (~0.6–0.9 m, head out of view, oriented toward the basin) stand behind their brighter right arm (~0.4–0.5 m), which rises closer to the camera in frame 2, exits the top of the frame in frame 3 as the wearer's right hand stays lowered inside the basin, and descends back to the basin rim (~0.15–0.2 m from the wearer's right hand) in frames 4–5. Compared to the visually busy and specular RGB strip, the depth map makes it much easier to see the vertical separation of the three hands floating over the basin and the receding depth of the second person's draped garment. However, the map is unreliable inside the reflective steel basin—where the concave interior, small inner cup, and sliced onions are flattened into a smooth gradient—and it merges the wearer's left hand and white cotton bundle into a single indistinct blob.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates discrete foreground regions within arm's reach (~0.3–0.8 m), most consistently tracking the camera wearer's right hand and forearm (pink 'person' mask on the right at ~0.35–0.5 m) as it moves from the basin's right edge in frame 1 into the inner cup across frames 2–5. In frames 1 and 5, brown and blue 'person' masks on the upper left capture the second person's striped garment (~0.6–0.9 m) and right arm (~0.4–0.5 m) reaching down from out of frame toward the basin, separated by ~0.15–0.25 m from the wearer's hands. In frames 2 and 4, a circular green 'bowl' mask (~0.5–0.6 m) delineates the large steel basin on the wearer's lap, clearly showing how the wearer's pink right-hand mask overlaps and occludes the right side of the basin. While these masks help demarcate the boundary between the wearer's reaching arm and the reflective bowl beneath it, the segmentation map is highly unreliable and temporally erratic across the 5 frames. It completely misses the steel basin in frames 1, 3, and 5, floods the background floor and chair (~1.2–1.8 m) with a single 'dining table' mask in frame 2, and mislabels the second person's torso as a 'bird' (frame 3) and the lower-left basket (~0.7 m) as a 'donut' (frame 3) and 'banana' (frame 5).
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders sparse 2D magenta hand skeletons and yellow body lines on a black background, capturing only partial detections in frames 1, 2, and 5 while leaving frames 3 and 4 completely blank. In frame 1, two magenta hand skeletons (~0.4–0.5 m from the camera and ~0.2 m apart) show the second person's downward-pointing right hand at the upper-left rim of the basin and the camera wearer's right hand forming a pinch on the right, and in frame 5 a single magenta skeleton captures the second person's right hand after it re-enters from the upper left and lowers back to the rim. Although neither person's head or gaze is visible in the downward-looking camera view, the articulated finger keypoints in frames 1 and 5 make the palm orientation and finger extension of the second person's descending hand and the wearer's initial pinch clearer than in the motion-blurred RGB frames. However, the pose map is largely unreliable across the sequence: it fails to detect the wearer's cotton-holding left hand on the left (~0.3–0.4 m) in every frame and misses the wearer's right hand inside the basin from frame 2 onward. Furthermore, in frames 1 and 2 it hallucinates miniature yellow upper-body and facial skeletons directly over the hands and steel basin (~0.5 m) where no head or torso exists.
